prompt_en: An editorial fashion photograph gives a new portrait frame to one visible person in a quiet city pause just after rain. The photograph captures the person's fashion look at the glass end of a transit shelter as the bus they were waiting for pulls away through the wet dusk. The supplied portrait guides the visible face and hair: large dark eyes, straight brows, a softly rounded nose, and full lips; a dark straight chin-length bob with a center part and airy fringe. The new composition places the person in a full-length urban scene. Their three-quarter turn follows the receding bus lights. The person stands by their own choice: stay for the next route or walk on. A long, sharply tailored cobalt-blue raincoat hangs open over a muted plum knit and charcoal wide-leg trousers, with dark leather shoes planted on the rain-polished pavement. One planted leg supplies the principal visible support; the free leg has a different relaxed or lightly contacting role; the pelvis and torso remain connected over the support base. A small draft from the bus lifts one side of the coat hem without breaking the person's steady stance. Amber shop light brushes one lapel and one cheek, then repeats as a slender stripe in the shelter glass; the glass also holds a broken reflection of the cobalt silhouette. The reflected figure and real figure stay aligned as the bus windows smear horizontally behind them, setting stillness against continued motion. A vertical eye-level view from across the lane keeps face, outfit, both shoes, reflection, shelter edge and a ribbon of wet curb together, with natural proportions. Focus holds on the person and the double silhouette while the bus and traffic recede softly into blue-gray dusk.
